implementation.what_the_patch_does: Under GGML_SCHED_EVAL_KEPT=1 and with an eval callback set: (1) when a graph is split for allocation, every node gets the output mark, so the allocator neither frees a node's memory nor lets a later node compute over it (dependencies/llama.cpp-f089c9c/ggml/src/ggml-alloc.c, the two checks of GGML_TENSOR_FLAG_OUTPUT); (2) a split is asked node by node as the installed branch asks it, and is given to the backend in as few ranges as its graph allows: a range ends only before a node that computes in place into the memory of an output wanted earlier (a node that is a view of the same tensor and is not a plain view, reshape, permute or transpose), and, when a split's nodes were not all marked (a graph allocated before the callback was set), after each wanted output as the installed branch does; a split with no such node is given whole, by the same call the scheduler makes when no callback is set; (3) at each range's end the outputs wanted so far are copied to host memory on the backend's own queue, the backend is waited for once a split, and the callbacks then read the copies, in the order the installed branch calls them; a callback that writes into its tensor or asks to stop aborts. The marks are set without asking the callback: the recorder's callback counts a microbatch when it is asked about the token rows (observe_stream.cpp, the embd row), so an extra question at allocation would change its records. Without the variable the library takes the installed branch.
implementation.processor_test: records/development/2026-11-10-speed-review/recorder-kept/eval_kept_test.cpp and eval_kept_test.txt: on the processor backend, 21 of 21 wanted outputs are the installed path's bytes under the kept path, in a graph whose memory the allocator reuses and where four nodes compute in place into a wanted output (5 ranges where the installed path takes 21; with the callback set after the allocation, 21 ranges and the same bytes); a kept callback that writes into its tensor or asks to stop aborts
implementation.identities: The sha256 named in this block are what a call is held to, by the comparison itself and not only by run.sh before the wait for the card: recorder_kept.py reads recorder_sha256, installed_library_sha256, kept_library_sha256, recorder_kept_py_sha256, recorder_deferred_py_sha256 and recorders_beside_py_sha256 (the two files it imports from) from this file and model_sha256 from above, hashes each of those files again before every one of the eight calls, and starts no call when one of them is not the declared bytes. Each process's mapped libggml-base.so.0 is held to the file hashed before its call by its inode, as the process's own map gives it, and that file is held to the declared sha256 again when the call has ended. No expectation is ever taken from a file as it stands.

hypothesis: The project's hypothesis: a capability leaves a recurring difference between the traces of correct and wrong answers, and editing the weights where that recurring difference lives repairs the capability. This run tests no part of it. It asks two questions of the instrument every step of a correction loop pays for: whether the recorder writes each answer's files with the bytes it writes today when the engine computes a split as one graph and the wanted outputs are read after it, and whether that takes less time; and it reads the engine's own count of its graph launches on both sides, so that where a kept token's time goes is measured and not left to a subtraction.
why_this_direction: Steps 1 and 2 of the method are the overlaps of the full traces, and step 5 measures the computation again on the current model's own answers after every update: each such measurement is the engine's capture of the thirty fitting answers, and under Astra's choice of November 15 that capture is the measured loss at every step. The capture is about three quarters of a gradient step as priced (223 s of about 4.5 minutes; speed review, 'A step taken by the gradient'), and the recorder's generation is nearly all of the capture. Three ways to shorten the generation with its bytes kept have been measured: the recorder's own bookkeeping is 2.2 to 2.4 ms of a kept token; recorder processes side by side are slower (runs/recorders-beside-original/result.json); and taking the 212 waits a token once a split gives the same bytes and 4% (runs/recorder-deferred-original/result.json: 13.432 against 13.972 ms a step). That last result leaves about 4 ms of a kept token that is neither the plain decode with its scores (7.9 ms) nor the recorder's records and callbacks (1.4 to 1.6 ms), and it kept one thing of the installed path unchanged: the split is still given to the card in 212 ranges a token. By the source, the card backend keys a graph by its first node, its node count and its end shapes (dependencies/llama.cpp-f089c9c/ggml/src/ggml-cuda/ggml-cuda.cu, ggml_cuda_graph_get_key), so each range is checked, captured once and replayed as a graph of its own, where the plain decode replays one. Whether those ranges are what the 4 ms pays for is not shown by a subtraction of times measured at other loads (Astra's reading of the result). This run is the next step because it removes the ranges and nothing else, with the bytes held, and reads the engine's own launch counter beside it: if the time falls, the ranges were the cost; if it does not, the counter says how many launches a token there are and what each costs on the host, and the ranges are closed as a lever with numbers.
repeating_pattern_check: Four things have happened more than once. (1) A faster way to read turned out to be another computation: thirty-two tokens at once, the second card, the torch forward. Why: the engine's kernels or their order differed. Here the order of nodes is the installed one and kernel fusion is off on both sides (own_text.py sets GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_FUSION=1, under which ggml_cuda_try_fuse returns at once), so each node is computed by its own kernel whether the graph is given whole or in ranges; but the card backend is a fork with rewrites of its own beside fusion, and it reads the output mark at seven places, so whether it does anything else differently for a whole graph of marked nodes is not known from reading. It is not taken on the argument: every answer's four files are held by sha256 to the installed recorder's in the same run, and one file apart closes it whatever its time. (2) A time priced as arithmetic stood where a measurement was wanted, and was wrong or uninformative: side by side was priced at 1.4 to 2.0 and measured 0.72; the deferred read-back was given a range of 9.3 to 15.0 ms and landed at 13.4, which showed the waits were not the cost and left what is the cost to a subtraction. Why: the parts on record did not separate what the arrangement itself costs. Here the prediction is again a range that includes no gain, and the engine's own counters (its graph launches and their host duration on both sides; the patched scheduler's splits, ranges and outputs) are read so that either outcome says where the time is. (3) A recorder's milliseconds a step were compared between two runs and differed by a tenth with the machine's load (13.97 in recorder-deferred-original against about 15.6 an hour before). The two sides alternate call by call under one hold of the lock, and only the sides of this run are compared. (4) Something a run depended on was not in its record: recorder-deferred-original did not record what host memory its copies were staged in (by the source it is the card backend's pinned memory when a process's first staged output is on the card's split; its record cannot show it). This patch prints the memory's name when it takes it, and the comparison keeps it.
what_went_wrong_before: Every construction so far repaired some answers and broke others, and the repeated correction on state values was stopped in its first pass. A step of a loop was 1 h 35 to 2 h in the on-policy loop and 44 to 52 minutes as the stopped loop's launcher stood; Marcos expects minutes. Under the gradient step Astra specified the capture is the largest part of a step, and the three measured attempts at its generation (the recorder's bookkeeping, recorders side by side, the waits taken once) found 4% between them.
rule: Data roles: the thirty fitting answers of the cohort controlled-bf16-1 (tube.picks) and no others. The answers no fit uses are not generated, read or listed; the reserved folder is not opened. The model is the original file, read only. One step (`compare`), under one hold of card 0's lock: for each of the three calls of ten answers, in the selection's order, the recorder is run once as installed and once kept, own_text.py's recorder call argument for argument; then the first call's ten answers are run once more on each side with GGML_CUDA_TIME_LAUNCH=1. Before every one of the eight calls the recorder, the two libraries, the comparison's own file and the two files it imports from are hashed and held to the sha256 this declaration names, and a file that is not the declared bytes starts no call; each process's library is read from its own map while it runs and held, by its inode, to the file hashed before its call, which is hashed again when the call has ended; a kept process must also carry the scheduler's line in its log and an installed one must not; a call that did not run the declared library of its side ends the comparison there. Each answer's stream.f32, stream.jsonl, result.json and case.json are hashed, kept against installed, in all four pairs of calls. A call's record is written first; then both streams of each answer whose four files are the same bytes are removed (the same command makes them again), and an answer with one file apart keeps both streams whole beside the record that names the files. A comparison is a count of equal bytes; no tolerance, threshold or score exists in this run. The seconds of the two timed calls enter no time reported for the sides. What the engine and the patched scheduler print of themselves (launches and their mean host duration a device; splits, ranges, outputs read back, splits not marked, the staging memory's name) is recorded as printed and starts or stops nothing. Nothing an answer says is compared or judged. The comparison is made once: what one that failed left is not touched. The research verifier runs before the step. The run writes only in its own folder. Whatever it finds, no instrument and no protocol is changed by it: the installed engine, the recorder and controlled-bf16-7 stay as they are, and a capture that uses the kept library is a separate acceptance.

prediction.1_bytes: 30 of 30 answers' four files have the same sha256 on both sides, and 10 of 10 in the timed pair. Held with less confidence than recorder-deferred-original's: there the card computed the same ranges in the same order; here it is given a split whole, with every node marked as an output and none computed in place over another. With fusion off each node is still computed by its own kernel in the installed order, and on the processor backend 21 of 21 wanted outputs were the installed path's bytes, four of them computed into in place later; what the card backend's own handling of a whole graph does to a kept output is what this measures.
prediction.2_time: the installed side: about 14.0 ms a step, as it stood in runs/recorder-deferred-original an hour before (13.972), and it moves with the machine's load. The kept side: between 9.3 and 13.4 ms a step, not known closer before it is measured. The lower end is the plain decode with its scores (7.9 ms) and the recorder's records and callbacks (1.4 to 1.6 ms; recorders-beside/bookkeeping.txt), if the ranges are all of what is left and copying 212 outputs after the graph costs nothing. The upper end is the deferred side's 13.432 ms, if the ranges were never the cost.
prediction.3_counts: the kept side's scheduler: no split not marked, and ranges a split near one (exactly one for a split with no node that computes in place into a wanted output; this model's graph is not known to have one, and the count says it). The engine's launch counter on the kept side: about one launch a generated step, as a plain decode has; on the installed side: either about 212 a generated step, if each range is replayed as a captured graph of its own as its key suggests, or few, if ranges are computed without replay. Which of the two it is, and the mean host duration it prints, is not predicted: no record holds it.

would_weaken_it: Nothing here bears on the hypothesis. On the instrument: (1) one file of one answer with other bytes on the kept side means the card does not compute a kept output from a whole graph of marked nodes as it does from the installed ranges: the variant is another computation as far as the record goes and is closed whatever its time; both streams are kept, and the labels that differ say where. (2) A kept side that is not faster (the median of an answer's kept seconds over its installed seconds at or above 1), with ranges a split near one, means the 212 ranges are not what a kept token pays for either: the lever is closed with its number, and the launch counter's two sides say what the installed path's launches cost. (3) Ranges a split far above one, or splits not marked, mean the variant did not compute a split as one graph on this model: its time then says nothing about one graph, and the count says why (nodes that compute in place, or graphs allocated before the callback was set).
inputs_read_for_what: The model is read by the recorder and never written. The cohort's declaration, the registered membership, the inputs' index and the wide overlap's members give the thirty fitting answers, their prompts' tokens and their limits (ladder.cohort, tube.picks, cases.chosen), as own_text.py takes them. The instruments (the recorder, the kept library, its patch and the comparison with the two files it imports from) are named under implementation with their sha256.

answers.derivation: tube.picks over the cohort's sixty answers: every other answer of each original outcome group, in the answers' own order, 15 correct and 15 wrong; none chosen by anything read here
answers.scales_with: the cohort's answers and their outcome labels

answers_a_call.derivation: 10: own_text.py gives the recorder ten answers a call, and the comparison calls the recorder as the capture does

order_of_the_sides.derivation: within each call the installed side runs first and the kept side second, and the calls follow one another, so the two sides alternate under one hold of the card's lock: neither has the first minutes of the card to itself, and a wait for the lock is in neither side's seconds. Nothing of an answer chooses its side: both sides generate every answer. It is recorder-deferred-original's order, so the installed side of the two runs is called the same way

faster.derivation: read from the times each answer's result.json was written on each side: an answer's seconds is the time from the end of the answer before it in its call, and a call's first answer has none (it holds the model's load). Reported: the milliseconds a step on each side (the seconds of the answers that have seconds on both sides, over their steps), the median, least and most of an answer's kept seconds over its installed seconds, and each call's whole seconds on each side. It is a measurement, not a gate: no value of it starts or stops anything in this run
faster.scales_with: the answers a call and their steps

timed_answers.derivation: the first call's ten answers, the first ten of the selection's order, once more on each side with the engine's launch timer: one call of the capture's own size, enough for the engine's running mean (it prints every 64 launches) and chosen by nothing read here. The timer adds two clock readings a launch and a line every 64, so these two calls' seconds are kept out of the sides' times

staging_chunk.derivation: 64 MiB of host memory a chunk in the patched scheduler, as in recorder-deferred-original's: the most one split's wanted outputs take is the prefill's microbatch, which that record gives as 32 tokens at once, times the 212 kept outputs, each 1,536 float32 wide: 41.7 MB, and 64 MiB is the next power of two above it. It bounds nothing: an output larger than what is left of a chunk takes the next chunk, and one larger than a chunk gets a chunk of its own size, so no byte of any output depends on it
staging_chunk.scales_with: the microbatch, the model's width and the kept outputs
